# Build journal — 2026-11-18

**Task:** WF-2 alert "LeadSimple CRM delivery failed" on the owner's smoke test
(submission 902d7bff-…, 11:46 UTC).

## What happened
- LeadSimple answered POST /deals with HTTP 429 (rate limited). Its limit is
  per ACCOUNT, 1-minute window (100 requests / 1000 records), shared with every
  other integration on that account.
- WF-2 did not see a 429. The alert read "POST /deals failed: Request failed
  with status code 429", with no "(HTTP 429)": the status was read as 0.
- The lead was not lost: it is stored by the gateway, and WF-2 sent the
  email-parse fallback and the team notification.

## Root cause (verified)
- The "CRM API attempt (mapped)" Code node runs in n8n's task runner
  (`N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED`). n8n 2.44.4 forwards `this.helpers.httpRequest` to
  the main process and sends a thrown error back as JSON
  (`task-requester.js` handleRpc: `data: e`).
- axios 1.20 `toJSON` keeps only message, name, stack, config, code, status.
  `e.response` (status, headers, body) does not survive. Reproduced locally
  with a real axios 1.20 429.
- So status = 0 -> treated as a dropped connection: a read-back GET before each
  retry (more quota spent), retries after 2s and 8s (same 1-minute window), and
  `X-RateLimit-Retry-After` was unreadable.
- The tests stubbed in-process errors (with `e.response`), which is why they
  stayed green.

## Fix
- POST /deals uses `ignoreHttpStatusErrors: true`, so a non-2xx is RETURNED
  with status, headers and body intact; the node turns it into the same error
  shape the retry logic already handled.
- Status also read from `e.status` (the wire shape) as a second line.
- A 429 without a server wait now waits 60s (the whole window), not 2s/8s.
  Server waits are capped at 90s so the worst case (2 x 90s + 3 x 10s) stays
  inside the 300s `N8N_RUNNERS_TASK_TIMEOUT`.
- Alert and config messages no longer say "main AND worker" (no worker since
  2026-11-11).
- Tests: 7 new ones model the real runner error shape. 9 fail on the old
  workflow, all 163 pass now.

## Open
- What used the LeadSimple quota at 11:46 is unknown. The deposit app's
  LeadSimple reads ran at 11:41 and 11:48, not 11:46. Other integrations on the
  same LeadSimple account (Zapier, native integrations) are candidates.
- The workflow must be re-imported/published in n8n to take effect.

## Second finding: a repeat guide request lost the contact
- Retest at 12:24 with the same email reached WF-2 with `email: ""`. The
  gateway's once-per-24h guide rule (westromhub1 `api/src/routes/leads.ts`)
  forwarded repeats WITHOUT contact, to avoid a second email and a duplicate
  deal. Effect: the 11:46 lead (deal failed on the 429) could never reach the
  CRM again that day, and any real owner returning within 24h got no deal.
- Owner decision (2026-11-18, "fix it"): a missing deal is worse than a
  duplicate one. The gateway now keeps the contact and sends
  `send_guide: false`; WF-1 carries it; WF-2 skips only the guide email and
  notes it in the deal comments. Absent `send_guide` means send, so the n8n
  side is safe to deploy first.
- Canonical schema change: one optional field, `send_guide` (boolean).

## Fallback path (email-parse) is not a deal path
- 11:46: Brevo accepted the parse email (messageId returned), but no deal
  appeared in LeadSimple. LeadSimple's conversation count rose by 2 right
  after, so the email most likely landed as an inbox conversation. Treat it
  as best-effort; the alert and the team notification carry the full lead.
